agency_full: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (lead) / European Space Agency (Huygens probe) / Agenzia Spaziale Italiana (high-gain antenna + radar)
payload: Saturn orbiter (~5712 kg dry) + Huygens descent probe (~318 kg, ESA-built, landed on Titan 2005-01-14)
credit: © NASA / JPL-Caltech / ESA / ASI / Space Science Institute — joint U.S. / European public-domain mission. Cassini orbited Saturn for 13 years (2004-2017), completing 294 orbits and 162 close moon flybys. Highlights: Huygens landed on Titan 2005-01-14 (first soft landing in the outer solar system); discovered Enceladus's plumes 2005 (~100 geysers from the south-polar tiger stripes); resolved Saturn's hexagonal polar storm; mapped Titan's lake system via radar; first observation of seasonal change on Saturn (Cassini covered nearly half a Saturnian year). Grand Finale (2017-04-23 to 2017-09-15) — 22 ring-gap orbits + atmospheric entry that destroyed the spacecraft over Saturn's cloud tops, ending the mission for planetary-protection reasons (preventing future biological contamination of Enceladus or Titan).

events.label: Launch
events.description: Titan IVB / Centaur lifts the 5712 kg Cassini–Huygens stack from Cape Canaveral toward a 6.7-year VVEJGA cruise — too heavy for a direct shot at Saturn, so four planetary gravity assists do the work the chemical engine cannot.

events.label: Venus #1 — gravity assist
events.description: First of four assists (1998-04-26). Cassini sweeps 284 km above Venus, stealing 7 km/s of orbital velocity from the planet to raise its aphelion outward. Total mission ∆v is fixed; this exchange is what makes Saturn reachable.

events.label: Venus #2 — gravity assist
events.description: Second Venus encounter (1999-06-24), 600 km altitude, after a Deep Space Manoeuvre that re-shaped the orbit. The two Venus assists together raise the aphelion past Earth, setting up the third assist 55 days later.

events.label: Earth — gravity assist
events.description: 1171 km above the South Pacific (1999-08-18) — the closest planetary flyby of any outbound interplanetary mission to date. The orbit is now energetic enough to cross Jupiter's, where the final assist will deliver Saturn.

events.label: Jupiter — gravity assist
events.description: 9.7 million km from Jupiter on 2000-12-30, simultaneous joint observation with Galileo (in Jovian orbit). Jupiter's gravity bends the trajectory the last 2.5 km/s needed to ride a Hohmann-like transfer to Saturn 3.6 years later.

events.label: Saturn orbit insertion
events.description: 96-minute main-engine burn (2004-07-01) slows the spacecraft from 30.5 km/s hyperbolic to 23.7 km/s, capturing into a 116-day orbit. The 13-year Saturn tour begins. Huygens will release toward Titan five months later.
